what_happened: Confirmed orchestrator-postflight.sh and skill_lifecycle_notify are orphaned for core task types (general/meta/markdown route directly to agents, bypassing the lifecycle-skill layer); this corroborates and explains why hooking the fix into claude-stop-notify.sh's Stop hook is structurally correct rather than a narrower lifecycle-notify.sh fix.

Discovered that lifecycle-notify.sh's .claude/tmp/orchestrate-active marker (described in its own header as the mid-orchestrate TTS suppressor) has zero writers anywhere in the source store -- dead code, separate from the genuinely live workflow-active-<uuid> marker. This is a second gap in the same file the dispatch already requires reconciling; folded into the Recommendations section rather than opened as separate work.

No existing scripts/tests/ file touches claude-stop-notify.sh, tts-notify.sh, or lifecycle-notify.sh at all, and no existing check asserts Notification-matcher parity between merge-sources/settings-hooks.json and root-files/settings.json. Acceptance criteria 2/3/4/6 all require new test/check coverage from scratch, not an extension of existing coverage.

Premise re-validation found all four carried-figure lines still exactly true against the live source store: claude-stop-notify.sh line 86-90 fires wezterm only with the quoted inline comment; lifecycle-notify.sh header lines 27-29 carry the contradicting decision table; both merge-sources/settings-hooks.json:64 and root-files/settings.json:188 declare permission_prompt|elicitation_dialog; tts-notify.sh has no cooldown state. No re-diagnosis needed, plan authored directly from the confirmed state.

Plan authoring surfaced a fact neither the description nor the research report states: the loader merge engine is additive-only, so widening the Notification matcher string yields a deployed settings.json carrying BOTH the old and new matcher blocks until the orphan sweep lands. An idle_prompt then matches one block and a permission_prompt matches both. This makes the cooldown a hard ordering prerequisite for the matcher widening, which the plan encodes as Phase 2 depends on Phase 1.

validate-artifact.sh's Tier-Justification suite-claim check reports a false 'fabricated claim' warning for any phase that edits an existing file and creates that file's new test suite in the same phase: the not-yet-existing test path is unmappable, which escalates suite_selection_select's whole multi-path call to __FULL_SWEEP__ by its fail-safe direction, so a measured suite list reads as fabricated. Three phases of this plan trip it. Default mode still exits 0; --strict exits 1. Worked around by stating the measured single-path result plus the escalation reason inside each justification and documenting it in the plan, rather than splitting tests away from the code they cover.
